_note: ONE TARGET, THREE BOARD NODES. 170:41's band is an instance of the shared
`Section header` component: a group (220:947 — 28 tall, 16 gutters, an 8
gap), an absolutely-positioned tint child (bg-subtle) and a label child
(11/16 ink-muted). The code draws that as one flex row, so all three join
to the same anchor.
THE BAND IS ALL THIS STATE HAS, and that is the finding, not a shortcut.
`useAgentRunner.start()` clears `steps`, awaits the plan, then sets the
steps and flips to phase "running" in the same breath — so `phase ===
"planning"` NEVER renders a step row. The board draws three pending rows
under the band and an `Edit plan` / `Run 3 steps` action row beneath them,
i.e. a plan-level review gate.
THAT GATE IS NOT BUILT HERE, on purpose. It is a new FSM state, and the
record already says so: LEDGER J-170:41 (2026-09-02) — the PRD documents
per-step approval only (11-flows.md:111-112, and board 170:97 draws that
shape), no chapter defines a plan-level gate, and the proposal is `add it
to 02:48 first, then code; otherwise redraw 170:41`. It was then routed to
the designer/founder lane as a structural redraw (LEDGER `designer-redraws`,
D9). Building it from a conformance pass would put a new approval step in
front of every agent run on the strength of a picture. So: band conformed,
gate left to the founder, and the three step rows measured on `ai-done`,
where the product does render them.
Also not built: `Edit plan` implies an editable plan, and there is no plan
editor, no state for one and no endpoint behind it.
